messages:
maria: Heads-up — running model bring-up benchmarks for redwood-llm-beta-3 on same SKU (A100-80GB) across AWS us-west-2, GCP us-west1, Azure westus3. Seeing consistent throughput but a weird ~20-35% p95 latency delta on Azure vs others. Anyone seen a cross-cloud L3/memory stall like this?

kevin: hmm. first suspects: driver minor versions and cuda toolkit patchlevel. also kernel scheduler and MMIO timeouts on azure VMs used before. did you capture nvidia-smi and uname?

maria: yeah, ps. quick outputs: ```
AWS (us-west-2): driver 535.54.03, cuda 12.2, kernel 5.15.0-101
GCP (us-west1): driver 535.54.03, cuda 12.2, kernel 5.15.0-102
Azure (westus3): driver 535.60.11, cuda 12.2, kernel 5.15.0-107
```

maria: full perf sample attached to bench dashboard (link in convo): https://internal/bench/1968/redwood-llm-beta-3 (bench-bot posted).

bench-bot: dashboard snapshot -> throughput p50/p95 + kernel counters (L2/L3) for each provider. quick summary: Azure shows higher L2 writeback stalls and elevated TLB refill counts during decode phase. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jonathan: elevated TLB refills suggests either different page table layout (hugepages) or NUMA mapping differences at boot. Did you provision with transparent hugepages or set hugetlbfs? Also check cudnn/cublas kernel selection — cublasLt path differs with driver microversions.

maria: we turned transparent hugepages off on all clusters. hugetlb not used. here's a short nvprof-like capture of the forward pass on Azure: ```
Kernel: gemm_int8_forward    calls: 24   avg_ms: 2.8   p95_ms: 6.2
Kernel: aten_conv           calls: 12   avg_ms: 1.1   p95_ms: 2.9
KV cache copy (host->device) p95 spikes at 8.1ms vs 2.2ms on AWS
```

kevin: KV copy p95 difference smells like PCIe/NUMA binding or host->device DMA engine contention. Are instances using the same CPU topology and PCIe root complex on Azure? Also check iommu and vfio settings.

tasha: Azure hypervisor recently rolled out updated firmware for that SKU in westus3; we've seen PMQoS changes affecting DMA batching. I can check with infra if the instances are on the new firmware pool. Also run pci_topology: ```
$ lspci -tv | sed -n '1,40p'
|-+-[0000:00]-+-00.0  Intel Corporation...
| `-1c.0  PCI bridge to [bus 01]
|-+-[0000:01]-+-00.0  NVIDIA Corporation...
```

maria: good call. I also tried forcing cublasLt -> cutlass path via env var (CUTLASS_DISABLE=0 / export CUBLAS_LT_ALGO_TEMP_DISABLE=1) and saw p95 drop ~12% on Azure. So kernel selection matters. But the KV p95 host->device remains worse.

jonathan: for bisect: 1) reproduce minimal repro (single-stream decode loop) with pinned numactl --cpunodebind and --membind toggles, 2) toggle hugepages and iommu on/off, 3) force driver 535.54.03 on Azure (if allowed) vs 535.60.11 and compare, 4) run dmabuf PCIe stress test (fio-like) to see host->device path.

maria: I'll run bisect tomorrow. Quick helpers I used: ```
# capture page map stats
$ perf stat -e page-faults,minor-faults,major-faults -a sleep 10

# measure H2D micro-latency
$ python micro_h2d.py --batch 1 --iters 10000 --pin
```

kevin: also check kernel dmesg for IOMMU or aspm warnings. azure firmware change left some hosts with aspm_enabled=false which increased latency in our past case.

tasha: pinged infra to identify firmware cohort and image id for the instances you used, maria. will post mapping. :mag_right:

maria: thanks. last note — quantized int8 path picks different cuBLAS heuristics; when I force float16 kernels, latency evens out across providers. suggests two-level effect: kernel heuristics + host->device DMA variance.

maria: will run the bisect matrix (driver, hugepages, numa binding, firmware cohort, kernel selector) and paste results here. thanks all. :pray:
